{{Elections in Ohio sidebar}}

The '''2026 Ohio Attorney General election''' was held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[attorney general of Ohio]]. [[John Kulewicz]] narrowly defeated his Republican opponent, State Auditor [[Keith Faber]]. <ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/other/kulewicz-announced-winner-in-ohio-attorney-general-race/ar-AA2gKpLV?ocid=BingNewsSerp |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-11-04 |title=Kulewicz announced winner in Ohio Attorney General race |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/kulewicz-announced-winner-ohio-attorney-171213428.html |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref> Kulewicz will succeed [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Andy Wilson (politician)|Andy Wilson]], who succeeded [[Dave Yost]] after his resignation. Yost was ineligible to seek a third consecutive term.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Tebben|first=Susan|date=May 16, 2025|title=Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost suspends campaign for governor|url=https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/briefs/ohio-attorney-general-dave-yost-suspends-campaign-for-governor/|work=[[Ohio Capital Journal]]|access-date=May 18, 2025}}</ref> This is the first time since 2009 a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] has been elected to the position in Ohio.   

[[Primary elections]] were held on May 5.

==Interim appointment==
On May 7, 2026, [[Dave Yost]] announced he would resign as attorney general effective June 7, 2026.<ref name=YostResigns>{{cite web |last1=Dennison |first1=J.W. |title=Gov. Mike DeWine accepts resignation from Attorney General Dave Yost |url=https://www.whiznews.com/gov-mike-dewine-accepts-resignation-from-attorney-general-dave-yost/ |website=[[WHIZ-TV]] |date=May 7, 2026 |access-date=May 7, 2026}}</ref> On May 11, 2026, Governor [[Mike DeWine]] announced that [[Andy Wilson (politician)|Andy Wilson]], the director of the [[Ohio Department of Public Safety]], would serve out the remainder of Yost's term.<ref name=WilsonAppointed />
